# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_scrape
definition.description:
Scrape one URL and return its content, or execute catalogued Alexandria capabilities. URL mode returns markdown by default, or HTML, links, screenshots, branding data, a targeted answer, or JSON matching a supplied schema, plus page metadata. Firecrawl may serve recently indexed content; set `maxAge: 0` for a live fetch. A successful response does not by itself confirm the page is still current. A named browser profile loads saved session data without saving changes to it.

`firecrawl_search` with `sources` unset and `firecrawl_find_tools` can discover providers for the same fields across several pages; a matching Alexandria provider returns typed records in one call.

Alexandria mode: `alexandria` selects catalogued capability execution and is mutually exclusive with `url`. Alexandria execution is billed at the capability's listed price and needs a team with Alexandria enabled.

profile.description: Loads a saved browser profile without saving changes to it.

requestId.description: Idempotency key bound to one Alexandria execution payload. Generated when omitted and returned with the result.

alexandria.description: Catalogued Alexandria capability invocation, mutually exclusive with url. One {provider, capability, options} object or an array of 1-10, with contracts available through firecrawl_search or firecrawl_find_tools. Each call may include version to pin a published workflow; omitting it uses latest. Only requestId and timeout are supported alongside alexandria. The selected contract marks required inputs and any requiresOneOf groups (at least one member per group); it may include example.request/example.response and response.key (which may differ from records). Where pagination is declared, its fields govern paging with the same filters; catalogue next is separate from provider pagination. Returns per-capability results in data.alexandria with data, records, or an error with a code; individual capabilities can fail even when the outer response succeeds. Requires an API key on a team with Alexandria enabled. Some providers require accepted terms; blocked requests return the applicable requirements.

capability.description: Capability address as returned by search or discover, e.g. "series/observations".

version.description: Optional published workflow version. Omit to use the latest version.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

options.description: Capability options as declared by its contract.

domainTools.description: URL mode only: include domain-matched Alexandria tools for the page in tools on the returned document. Ignored with alexandria.

definition.name: mcp__claude_ai_Firecrawl__firecrawl_search
definition.description:
Search web and specialized indexes, returning ranked results with query-relevant highlights. Each web result is a title, URL, and description. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. `includeDomains` and `excludeDomains` are mutually exclusive hostname filters; categories limit result types to `research`, `pdf`, `developer`, or `gov`.

For a programming question, add `categories: ["developer"]`. It searches an index of public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation, and returns the results in `data.web` with `category: "developer"`.

For a legal or regulatory question, `categories: ["gov"]` returns results in `data.web` with `category: "gov"` and cannot be combined with other categories; `firecrawl_gov_search` is the dedicated tool. Verify gov results' issuer, jurisdiction, status, and version before citing current law.

Authenticated search combines web results, semantic tool summaries and domain matches. Use sources: ["alexandria"] for semantic tools only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. Tool matches describe available structured-data capabilities, not executed data. toolDetail: "compact" (default) returns only provider, capability and description; "summary" adds metadata; "full" includes their input and output contracts. firecrawl_scrape with an alexandria body executes a selected capability; firecrawl_find_tools provides catalogue browsing and full contracts.

Returns result groups in `data` and an operation `id`.

toolDetail.description: Compact by default. Compact returns only provider, capability and description; full includes contracts. Inspect selected compact tools with firecrawl_find_tools providers and capabilities.

query.description: Query for web and semantic tool discovery. Operators include quoted phrases, `-term`, `site:host`, `inurl:term`, `intitle:term`, and `related:host`; the set is non-exhaustive. Catalogue browsing is available through firecrawl_find_tools.

domainTools.description: Include domain-matched tools for result URLs. Defaults to true when Alexandria is combined with web, news or images; semantic-only search leaves domain matching off.

highlights.description: Return query-relevant page excerpts for web and news results when available (default). Highlights appear in web `description` and news `snippet`; otherwise, original snippets are returned. Set to false to keep the original search snippets.

includeDomains.description: Hostnames to restrict results to. Mutually exclusive with excludeDomains.

excludeDomains.description: Hostnames to leave out of results. Mutually exclusive with includeDomains.

sources.description: Search sources; authenticated sessions default to web + alexandria, keyless sessions to web only. Authenticated searches always add alexandria to the sources, so sources: ["web"] also returns providers; domainTools: false turns off website-matched tools only. enterprise zdr or anon searches do not add it. Use ["alexandria"] alone for provider discovery without web results.

categories.description: Limit results to specific source types. `research` restricts ordinary web results to research-affiliated websites and returns page snippets, which is separate from the `firecrawl_research_*` tools that search paper abstracts and full text across biomedical (PubMed, bioRxiv, medRxiv) and arXiv literature; `pdf` searches PDF results; `developer` searches an index built for coding agents over public repositories, GitHub issues, merged pull requests, repository READMEs, and code documentation; `gov` searches the Government Index of US federal, state, and local legal and regulatory sources, the index behind firecrawl_gov_search, and cannot be combined with other categories; gov hits can include historical versions, bill text, agency guidance, and third-party reproductions, so verify the issuer, jurisdiction, enacted/effective status, and version before citing current governing law, clarify a missing jurisdiction or ambiguous as-of date, and use general search for non-US questions or missing coverage (no hits does not establish that no applicable law exists). `developer` and `gov` return hits in `data.web` with `category` set to their name; the other categories also filter `data.web`.

# New Telemetry traits and the young-player weight rule

Date: 2026-10-17. Status: **decisions recorded; build in 020.** Nothing in
019 changed.

## What Telemetry added

Read from the live leaderboard Columns panel (2026, all 11 groups, both tabs)
on 2026-10-17. Advanced Stats: no change. Player Traits: 7 new columns.

| Group | New Player Traits columns |
|---|---|
| OT, IOL | Pull Agility, Perimeter Speed |
| OB-LB | Closing, Reaction Time |
| CB, SAF | Targeted Coverage, Closing, Reaction Time |

Telemetry's own definitions (player-page tooltips):

| Trait | Definition |
|---|---|
| Pull Agility | Measures a lineman's ability to change direction and cut upfield as a puller. |
| Perimeter Speed | Measures a lineman's straight line speed. |
| Targeted Coverage | Measures the primary coverage defender's ability to stay in phase when targeted. |
| Closing | Measures a defender's ability to close on the ball when it's in the air, both as the primary and secondary defender. |
| Reaction Time | Measures how fast a secondary defender commits to the ball once it's thrown. |

LB tooltips were not read separately; assumed the same text.

**Sample size:** these traits are blank for many players. On the OT board,
4 of the top 15 have no Pull Agility / Perimeter Speed. One 2026 CB ranked
"14th of 36 in FBS" on Reaction Time, so very few players are scored.

## Effect on the pipeline today

- `check_exports.py` flags only missing columns, so the new columns pass.
- `scripts/powerquery/Stage.m` keeps only its known column list, so the new
  columns are dropped silently. Nothing breaks; nothing is used.

## Crosswalk (proposed; add as secondaries, not counted traits)

Counted traits drive elite share (same open question as Elusiveness), so
these go in as secondaries until that is decided.

| Group | Trait | Baylor factor (000 GRD SCALE) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| OT | Pull Agility | Athletic Ability | Factor had no Telemetry feed (no CoD/Decel for OL). |
| OT | Perimeter Speed | Speed (Play-speed) | Colleague proposed Foot speed / Redirect. The definition is straight-line speed, so Speed. Speed had no OL feed. |
| OG/C | Pull Agility | Pulling / 2nd level blocking | Direct match. |
| OG/C | Perimeter Speed | Speed (Play-speed) | As OT. |
| CB, STAR | Targeted Coverage | Man-to-Man Coverage | Direct match. |
| CB, STAR | Closing | Ball Skills | "Disruptive at rec. point." |
| CB, STAR | Reaction Time | Ball Skills (secondary) | No read/react factor on CB. |
| SAF | Reaction Time | Key & Diagnose | "Reads and reacts quickly." |
| SAF | Closing | Range | Plays to the sideline. |
| SAF | Targeted Coverage | none clean | Info only until staff decide. |
| LB | Closing | Lateral quickness / Range | Weak fit. |
| LB | Reaction Time | none | LB scale has no read/react factor. Info only. |

Defensive rows are proposed by Claude, not yet confirmed by Eric or staff.

## Weight rule for young players (Eric chose option 1, 2026-10-17)

Height stays the hard line. A player whose only size miss is weight below the
SETTINGS floor, with Elig. 3 or more, is flagged **PROJECT** instead of
scoring Size 1 (critical deficiency). Older players keep the current rule:
a light senior is not a project.

Before building: read the SIZE (data) formula in 019 to confirm how a
below-floor weight scores today (1 or 3). The 000 matrix weight columns were
unclear in the text export. `check_workbook.py` does not recompute SIZE, so
spot-check SIZE and the PROJECT flag on a few players per position.

## Build list for 020

1. Stage.m and POSITION MAP: add the 7 columns (OT, IOL, OB-LB, CB, SAF).
2. CROSSWALK / glossary: add the rows above, with the definitions.
3. SIZE: weight-only miss + Elig. >= 3 -> PROJECT, not 1.
4. `check_exports.py`: add the new columns to EXPECTED only after a full
   2023-2026 pull shows whether older seasons carry them.

# AGENTS.md

Project: PP_Recruiting (Baylor Football Player Personnel)

## What this is

A unified grading system for Baylor Football player personnel that couples
Telemetry (Teamworks) trait percentiles with the internal S.T.A.Q.S. grading
scale, so transfer-portal data gets filtered down to the players who deserve a
scout's time. The STAQS grade stays the grade of record. Telemetry data only
decides who gets reviewed. It never produces a competing grade.

## Two locations, know which is which

Workbooks, Word deliverables and the `Send/` folder live on Google Drive:

`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\02_SPORTS\Football\PP_Recruiting`

That folder holds the full project handoff in its own `AGENTS.md` and the
development history in `LOG.md`. Read both before doing work on the system
itself. They are the substantive spec. This repo is the version-controlled half:
documentation, decisions, and scripts.

An older copy of the project under `OneDrive - Baylor University` no longer
exists. Session logs and Codex rollouts that name that path are stale.

## Session routine

- Start: run `git pull`, then read `docs/STATUS.md` before doing anything else.
  Then read the Drive folder's `AGENTS.md` and `LOG.md`.
- End: update `docs/STATUS.md` (done, next, open questions), commit, and
  `git push`.
- Never leave uncommitted work at the end of a session.

## Conventions

- Durable notes and decisions go in `docs/`, committed. Not in chat.
- Workbooks, documents and data exports stay on Google Drive, not in this repo.
  Files over 95 MB never go in git.
- Telemetry and Teamworks are read-only. Navigate and read, never edit there.
- Writing: plain, direct, no em dashes. Documents use the Baylor design system.
- Deliverables on Drive are numbered in sequence. 013 is the latest, so the next

- The proposed Jev recruiting pilot is captured in
  `docs/2026-09-22-jev-recruiting-pilot.md`. It is a shadow-mode plan, not an
  approved workbook rule or a replacement for the weekly refresh.

## Standing rules carried over from the Drive handoff

- Threshold flags, never a weighted composite.
- Elite share, not raw elite count, because positions carry different trait
  counts (OL has 2, LB has 8).
- The data grades 4 of 5 critical factors, proxies Toughness, and never touches
  FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, or medical.
- Do not retry reading Telemetry's auth token or importing its internal service
  classes. Both are blocked. Scrape the rendered table instead.

// Stage: reads and checks every Telemetry leaderboard CSV in the export folder named on
// UPDATE DATA and returns a record { Rows, Status }. Port of
// scripts/load_leaderboard.py (read_csvs + build_rows); keep the two in step.
// Connection only; PortalInput and LoadStatus read from it.
let
    Cfg = (name as text) =>
        try Excel.CurrentWorkbook(){[Name = name]}[Content]{0}[Column1] otherwise null,

    RawPath = Cfg("LoadFolder"),
    PathText = if RawPath = null then "" else Text.Trim(Text.Trim(Text.From(RawPath)), """"),
    FolderPath =
        if PathText = "" then
            error Error.Record(
                "No export folder",
                "Paste the folder that holds the Telemetry CSVs into the yellow cell on the UPDATE DATA tab, then Refresh All.")
        else if Text.EndsWith(PathText, "\") then PathText
        else PathText & "\",

    MinEligRaw = Cfg("LoadMinElig"),
    MinElig = if MinEligRaw = null or MinEligRaw = "" then null else Number.From(MinEligRaw),

    // PORTAL INPUT row 4, columns A:BO. REVIEW BOARD reads these by position:
    // never reorder.
    Headers = {
        "Player", "Pos (Telemetry)", "Class", "Prev Team", "HT (in)", "WT", "Elig Yrs", "Snaps",
        "Snaps detail", "Hometown", "High School", "Entered", "Committed To", "Top End Speed (mph)",

        "Target Rate", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed", "Penalty", "Penalty Drawn", "Notes"},

    // CSV header -> PORTAL INPUT header, where the names differ.
    Aliases = {
        {"Pos.", "Pos (Telemetry)"}, {"Team", "Prev Team"}, {"Weight", "WT"}, {"Elig.", "Elig Yrs"},
        {"Top End Speed", "Top End Speed (mph)"}, {"Adj. Throw Velocity", "Adj Throw Vel"},

        {"Completion Rate Over Expected", "Comp Rate Over Expected"}, {"EPA/Target", "EPA Per Target"}},
    Special = {"Height", "Hometown", "State", "PlayerId", "Rank", "#"},

    // Leaderboard position code -> POSITION MAP code.
    PosMap = [

    TextColumns = {"Player", "Pos (Telemetry)", "Class", "Prev Team", "Snaps detail", "Hometown",
        "High School", "Entered", "Committed To", "Risk Level", "Notes"},

    // Required columns per (group, tab): generated from scripts/check_exports.py. Keep in step.
    Roster = {"PlayerId", "Rank", "Player", "#", "Pos.", "Class", "Elig.", "Height", "Weight", "Team", "Hometown", "State", "Snaps"},
    GroupCodes = [
        QB = {"QB"},

        TE = {"F", "H", "TE", "Y"},
        OT = {"LT", "OT", "RT", "T"},
        IOL = {"C", "G", "LG", "OG", "RG"},
        IDL = {"DL", "DT", "NT"},
        EDGE = {"DE", "DOWN", "EDGE", "UP"},
        #"OB-LB" = {"ILB", "LB", "OLB", "UP"},

        #"SAF|player-traits" = {"Play Speed", "Deep Speed", "Burst", "CoD", "Decel", "Tackling", "Run Defense"},
        #"QB|advanced-stats" = {"Player Impact", "Passing Production", "Passing Effectiveness", "Evasion Rate", "Batdowns", "Rushing Production", "Rushing Effectiveness", "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"},

        #"WR|advanced-stats" = {"Player Impact", "Receiving Production", "Receiving Effectiveness", "Separation", "YAC Over Expected", "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact", "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"},
        #"TE|advanced-stats" = {"Player Impact", "Receiving Production", "Receiving Effectiveness", "Stops Allowed Over Expected", "Disruption Prevention", "YAC Over Expected", "Tackles Avoided", "Yards After Contact", "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"},
        #"OT|advanced-stats" = {"Player Impact", "Push", "Stops Allowed Over Expected", "Disruption Prevention", "Penalty", "Movement"},
        #"IOL|advanced-stats" = {"Player Impact", "Push", "Stops Allowed Over Expected", "Disruption Prevention", "Penalty", "Movement"},
        #"IDL|advanced-stats" = {"Player Impact", "Run Stops Over Expected", "Push", "Disruption", "Double Team Rate", "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty", "Batdowns", "Screen Awareness", "Top End Speed"},
        #"EDGE|advanced-stats" = {"Player Impact", "Disruption", "Push", "Run Stops Over Expected", "Double Team Rate", "Penalty Drawn", "Penalty", "Batdowns", "Screen Awareness", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed"},

        #"CB|advanced-stats" = {"Player Impact", "EPA/Target", "Comp Rate Over Expected", "Ball Hawk", "Target Rate", "Penalty", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"},
        #"SAF|advanced-stats" = {"Player Impact", "EPA/Target", "Comp Rate Over Expected", "Ball Hawk", "Target Rate", "Penalty", "Top End Speed", "Adjusted Speed", "Power Speed"}
        ],

    // Column check (019): a column switched off in the leaderboard view is simply not
    // in the file, and Excel turns a saved Height "6-0" into "Jun-00". Port of
    // scripts/check_exports.py check_rows: group from Pos. codes (90%+ of rows), tab

    HeightOk = (h) =>
        let t = if h = null then "" else Text.Trim(Text.From(h)),
            p = Text.Split(t, "-")
        in t = "" or t = "-" or t = "---" or
           (List.Count(p) = 2 and Text.Length(p{0}) = 1 and Text.Length(p{1}) >= 1 and Text.Length(p{1}) <= 2
            and Text.Select(t, {"0".."9", "-"}) = t),
    CheckFile = (cols as list, rows as table) as list =>
        let
            codes = if List.Contains(cols, "Pos.") then
                    List.Transform(Table.Column(rows, "Pos."), each if _ = null then "" else Text.Trim(Text.From(_)))
                else List.Repeat({""}, Table.RowCount(rows)),
            total = List.Count(codes),

        in

            else (if List.IsEmpty(missing) then {} else {"missing " & Text.Combine(missing, ", ")})

                & (if badHeights > 0 then {Text.From(badHeights) & " unreadable heights (saved in Excel?)"} else {}),

    Num = (v) =>
        if v = null then null
        else if v is number then v
        else
            let s = Text.Trim(Text.From(v))
            in if s = "" or s = "-" or s = "---" then null
               else try Number.From(s, "en-US") otherwise s,

    HeightInches = (h) =>
        let
            parts = if h = null then {} else Text.Split(Text.Trim(h), "-")

            then try 12 * Number.From(parts{0}) + Number.From(parts{1}, "en-US") otherwise null

    AllFiles = Folder.Files(FolderPath),
    Csvs = Table.SelectRows(AllFiles, each
        Text.Lower([Extension]) = ".csv" and Text.Lower([Folder Path]) = Text.Lower(FolderPath)),
    FileList = Table.Buffer(Table.Sort(Table.SelectColumns(Csvs, {"Name", "Content"}), {{"Name", Order.Ascending}})),
    CheckedFiles =
        if Table.RowCount(FileList) = 0 then
            error Error.Record("No CSV files",
                "No .csv files in " & FolderPath & ". Download the Telemetry exports into that folder.")
        else FileList,

    Known = Headers & {"Elusiveness"},
    AliasFrom = List.Transform(Aliases, each _{0}),

    ParseFile = (name as text, content as binary, idx as number) =>
        let
            raw = Table.PromoteHeaders(
                Csv.Document(content, [Delimiter = ",", Encoding = 65001, QuoteStyle = QuoteStyle.Csv]),
                [PromoteAllScalars = true]),
            cols = Table.ColumnNames(raw),
            blanks = Table.Buffer(Table.TransformColumns(raw, {}, each if _ = "" then null else _)),
            withPid = Table.SelectRows(blanks, each Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "PlayerId") <> null
                and Text.Trim(Record.Field(_, "PlayerId")) <> ""),
            derived = Table.AddColumn(withPid, "__derived", each [
                PlayerId = Text.Trim([PlayerId]),
                #"Pos (raw)" = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Pos."),
                #"HT (in)" = HeightInches(Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Height")),
                Hometown =
                    let town = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "Hometown"),
                        st = Record.FieldOrDefault(_, "State"),
                        stt = if st = null then "" else Text.Trim(st)
                    in if town = null then null else if stt <> "" then town & ", " & stt else town]),
            renamed = Table.RenameColumns(Table.RemoveColumns(derived, List.Intersect({cols, Special})),
                List.Select(Aliases, each List.Contains(cols, _{0}))),
            keep = List.Select(Table.ColumnNames(renamed), each List.Contains(Known, _)),
            base = Table.SelectColumns(renamed, keep & {"__derived"}),
            expanded = Table.ExpandRecordColumn(base, "__derived",
                {"PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "HT (in)", "Hometown"},
                {"PlayerId", "Pos (raw)", "HT (in)", "Hometown"}),
            indexed = Table.AddIndexColumn(expanded, "__row", 0, 1),
            tagged = Table.AddColumn(Table.AddColumn(indexed, "__idx", each idx), "__file", each name)
        in
            [Table = tagged, Headers = cols, Name = name, Problems = CheckFile(cols, blanks)],

    Parsed = List.Transform(
        List.Positions(CheckedFiles[Name]),
        (i) => ParseFile(CheckedFiles{i}[Name], CheckedFiles{i}[Content], i)),

    Combined = Table.Buffer(Table.Combine(List.Transform(Parsed, each [Table]))),
    ValueCols = List.Difference(Table.ColumnNames(Combined), {"PlayerId", "__row", "__idx", "__file"}),

    // First non-blank value per column, in file-name order (as the Python loader).
    Grouped = Table.Group(Combined, {"PlayerId"}, {{"__rec", (g) =>
        let s = Table.Sort(g, {{"__idx", Order.Ascending}, {"__row", Order.Ascending}})
        in Record.FromList(
               List.Transform(ValueCols, (c) => List.First(List.RemoveNulls(Table.Column(s, c)))),
               ValueCols)
           & [#"Source files" = Text.Combine(List.Sort(List.Distinct(s[__file]), Comparer.Ordinal), "; ")]}}),
    Players = Table.FromRecords(
        List.Transform(Table.ToRecords(Grouped), each [PlayerId = [PlayerId]] & [__rec]),
        null, MissingField.UseNull),

    BenchmarkIds = List.Buffer(
        try Excel.CurrentWorkbook(){[Name = "BenchmarkIds"]}[Content][PlayerId] otherwise {}),

    Shaped = Table.FromRecords(
        List.Transform(Table.ToRecords(Players), (r) =>
            let
                rawPos = Record.FieldOrDefault(r, "Pos (raw)"),
                code = if rawPos = null then null else Record.FieldOrDefault(PosMap, rawPos, rawPos),
                withPos = r & [#"Pos (Telemetry)" = code],
                main = Record.FromList(
                    List.Transform(Headers, (h) =>
                        let v = Record.FieldOrDefault(withPos, h)
                        in if List.Contains(TextColumns, h) then v else Num(v)),
                    Headers),
                extra = [
                    PlayerId = r[PlayerId],
                    #"Pos (raw)" = rawPos,
                    Elusiveness = Num(Record.FieldOrDefault(r, "Elusiveness")),
                    #"Source files" = r[#"Source files"],
                    #"Benchmark 2025" = if List.Contains(BenchmarkIds, r[PlayerId]) then "BENCHMARK" else null]
            in main & extra),
        Headers & Extras),

    Kept = Table.SelectRows(Shaped, each
        MinElig = null or ([Elig Yrs] is number and [Elig Yrs] >= MinElig)),
    Sorted = Table.Sort(Kept, {
        {each if [#"Pos (Telemetry)"] = null then "" else Text.From([#"Pos (Telemetry)"]), Order.Ascending},
        {each if [Player] = null then "" else Text.From([Player]), Order.Ascending}}),

    AllHeaders = List.Distinct(List.Combine(List.Transform(Parsed, each [Headers]))),
    Unmapped = List.Select(AllHeaders, each
        not List.Contains(Known, _) and not List.Contains(AliasFrom, _) and not List.Contains(Special, _)),
    RawCodes = List.Distinct(List.RemoveNulls(Players[#"Pos (raw)"])),
    UnknownCodes = List.Select(RawCodes, each not Record.HasFields(PosMap, _)),

    Status = [
        Folder = FolderPath,
        Files = List.Count(Parsed),
        FileNames = Text.Combine(CheckedFiles[Name], "; "),
        PlayersRead = Table.RowCount(Players),
        RowsKept = Table.RowCount(Kept),
        Dropped = Table.RowCount(Players) - Table.RowCount(Kept),
        MinElig = MinElig,
        UnknownCodes = Text.Combine(UnknownCodes, ", "),
        Unmapped = Text.Combine(Unmapped, ", "),
        Benchmark = List.Count(List.Select(Kept[#"Benchmark 2025"], each _ <> null)),
        ProblemFiles = List.Count(List.Select(Parsed, each not List.IsEmpty([Problems]))),
        Problems = Text.Combine(List.Transform(List.Select(Parsed, each not List.IsEmpty([Problems])),
            each [Name] & ": " & Text.Combine([Problems], "; ")), " | ")]
in
    [Rows = Sorted, Status = Status]

content.content:
Five critical factors (all positions): **S**ize, **T**oughness, **A**thletic
Flexibility, **Q**uickness, **S**peed. Plus **3 position-specific** factors. QB
has its own set of 8.

Tiers (also loaded as the Player Grade dropdown in Telemetry Scout Reports >
Settings):

| Grade | Score | Elite traits | Color |
|---|---|---|---|
| AA | 60-72 | 7-8 | green `00B050` |
| AL | 48-59 | 5-6 | yellow `FFC000` |
| QS | 40-47 | 3-4 | black `404040` |
| FRP | 30-39 | 1-2 | grey `D8D8D8` |
| LIM | 24-29 | 0-1 | pink `ED6363` |
| NGE | 8-23 (dropdown 0-23) | 0 | red `C00000` |

---

## 5. The bridge (Telemetry to STAQS) — the core algorithm

Implement exactly this. Every constant lives on the workbook **SETTINGS** tab
and must stay editable there rather than hardcoded in formulas.

```
elite trait      := Telemetry percentile >= 75
deficiency       := Telemetry percentile < 25
graded traits    := traits with a numeric percentile for that player
elite share      := elite traits / graded traits
```

Elite share (not raw count) is used because positions carry different numbers of
Telemetry traits — OL has 2, LB has 8 — so a raw count would systematically
punish linemen.

Share maps to a projected band using the GRD SCALE's own elite-trait cut lines:

```
>= .875 (7/8) -> AA
>= .625 (5/8) -> AL
>= .375 (3/8) -> QS
>= .125 (1/8) -> FRP
   0          -> LIM, or NGE when deficiencies exceed elite traits by 2+
                 with no elite share
```

Guards and flags:

- **Minimum 2 graded traits** to project a band; otherwise the row is `THIN`.
- **REVIEW** fires at elite share >= .375 (the QS floor), or when the Speed
  alert or Impact alert fires, for any row with at least one graded trait.
- **Speed alert**: Play Speed or Deep Speed >= 90 ("documented difference making
  SPEED" on the GRD SCALE).
- **Impact alert** (009, decided 2026-09-16): Player Impact >= 90. Fires on its
  own and turns REVIEW on. Chosen after the validation run caught 6 of 13
  missed QS-or-better players at 90.
- **Low Impact alert** (009): a REVIEW row with Player Impact <= 10. A caution
  note only; it never removes REVIEW.
- **Size-Speed alert**: poor size with elite speed — the GRD SCALE's "must be
  special and offer a role" exception.
- **LOW SAMPLE** below 150 snaps. Telemetry itself blanks most traits under
  roughly 100 snaps.
- **Profile REVIEW** (013, decided 2026-09-26): the position's two must-haves
  (SETTINGS POSITION PROFILES) both at or above their floors, 200+ snaps, and
  the position's 2nd-path switch on (OT, OG, C, EDGE). Turns REVIEW on. A blank
  must-have counts as not cleared. Must-have status, Profile and the Diamond
  signal show for every position as information only.

**What data can and cannot grade.** Data directly supports 4 of the 5 critical
factors (Speed, Quickness, Athletic Flexibility, Size from HT/WT) and offers
proxies for Toughness. Position-specific factors get partial support (see the
CROSSWALK tab). FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, and medical are **never**
data-graded.

---

## 6. Workbook structure (003 layout; 010 is current, same layout as 009)

Tabs, in order:

- **README** — what it is, the bridge, how to use, scope, cell legend, sources.
- **SETTINGS** — thresholds (rows 5-12 in 009, including the two alert cut
  points at rows 11-12), band cut lines, simplified size standards by position.
  *All tuning happens here.*
- **GRADE SCALE** — the six tiers.
- **METRIC GLOSSARY** — what each Telemetry metric measures.
- **CROSSWALK** — which Telemetry metric informs which STAQS factor, by position.
- **POSITION MAP** — Telemetry position codes -> Baylor eval tabs -> trait counts.
- **PORTAL INPUT** — the data sheet, columns A:BO (67) plus PlayerId, raw
  position, Elusiveness and source file in BP:BS from 008 on. Grouped as Player
  Traits (all positions, P:AC) / QB Traits (AD:AI) / Advanced Stats (AJ:BN).
  Percentiles 0-100; blank where a position carries no metric. HT in inches
  (6'1" = 73). **REVIEW BOARD reads these columns by fixed position, not by
  header, so never insert, delete or reorder PORTAL INPUT columns.** Load data
  with `load_leaderboard.py`, which maps CSV headers onto the template's
  columns.
- **REVIEW BOARD** — all formulas, do not hand-edit. One row per PORTAL INPUT
  row. Columns: traits graded, elite traits, deficiencies, elite share,
  projected band, REVIEW?, speed alert, size-speed alert, Impact alert and Low
  Impact alert (N:O, 009), critical deficiency, data-suggested SIZE / TOUGH /
  ATHLETIC / QUICK / SPEED values, best and worst trait, plus roster metadata.

**Cell legend:** yellow fill `FFF2CC` with blue text = user input. Black text =
formula.

**House styling** (workbooks and companion docs both): Arial throughout unless
the Baylor-style variant is called for; titles Arial 12pt bold Baylor green
`154734`; subtitles and notes 9pt grey `595959`; table header rows white bold on
`154734`; tier fills per §4. The "Baylor style" variants (003 xlsx, 005 docx)
additionally use NCAA Baylor Bears / Baylor Bears Font display type and
Bahnschrift body, with a black masthead bar. Those fonts render only on a
machine that has them installed; Word substitutes elsewhere.

---

## 7. Telemetry platform notes

Telemetry Sports (app.telemetry.fm, branded Teamworks) is the recruiting and
scouting platform. Login is the user's; an agent without a browser session
cannot reach it.

- **Transfer Portal** > Player Traits / Advanced Stats / Boxscore. Traits and
  stats appear only after filtering to a position or position group.
- **Scout Reports > Settings** holds the Player Grade dropdown, already loaded
  with the six STAQS tiers. Scout reports carry a numeric Score (0-72) plus the
  grade.

- **Profile REVIEW** (013, decided 2026-09-26): the position's two must-haves
  (SETTINGS POSITION PROFILES) both at or above their floors, 200+ snaps, and
  the position's 2nd-path switch on (OT, OG, C, EDGE). Turns REVIEW on. A blank
  must-have counts as not cleared. Must-have status, Profile and the Diamond
  signal show for every position as information only.

**What data can and cannot grade.** Data directly supports 4 of the 5 critical
factors (Speed, Quickness, Athletic Flexibility, Size from HT/WT) and offers
proxies for Toughness. Position-specific factors get partial support (see the
CROSSWALK tab). FBI, wiring, keep-ability, character, and medical are **never**
data-graded.

---

## 6. Workbook structure (003 layout; 010 is current, same layout as 009)

Tabs, in order:

- **README** — what it is, the bridge, how to use, scope, cell legend, sources.
- **SETTINGS** — thresholds (rows 5-12 in 009, including the two alert cut
  points at rows 11-12), band cut lines, simplified size standards by position.
  *All tuning happens here.*
- **GRADE SCALE** — the six tiers.
- **METRIC GLOSSARY** — what each Telemetry metric measures.
- **CROSSWALK** — which Telemetry metric informs which STAQS factor, by position.
- **POSITION MAP** — Telemetry position codes -> Baylor eval tabs -> trait counts.
- **PORTAL INPUT** — the data sheet, columns A:BO (67) plus PlayerId, raw
  position, Elusiveness and source file in BP:BS from 008 on. Grouped as Player
  Traits (all positions, P:AC) / QB Traits (AD:AI) / Advanced Stats (AJ:BN).
  Percentiles 0-100; blank where a position carries no metric. HT in inches
  (6'1" = 73). **REVIEW BOARD reads these columns by fixed position, not by
  header, so never insert, delete or reorder PORTAL INPUT columns.** Load data
  with `load_leaderboard.py`, which maps CSV headers onto the template's
  columns.
- **REVIEW BOARD** — all formulas, do not hand-edit. One row per PORTAL INPUT
  row. Columns: traits graded, elite traits, deficiencies, elite share,
  projected band, REVIEW?, speed alert, size-speed alert, Impact alert and Low
  Impact alert (N:O, 009), critical deficiency, data-suggested SIZE / TOUGH /
  ATHLETIC / QUICK / SPEED values, best and worst trait, plus roster metadata.

**Cell legend:** yellow fill `FFF2CC` with blue text = user input. Black text =
formula.

**House styling** (workbooks and companion docs both): Arial throughout unless
the Baylor-style variant is called for; titles Arial 12pt bold Baylor green
`154734`; subtitles and notes 9pt grey `595959`; table header rows white bold on
`154734`; tier fills per §4. The "Baylor style" variants (003 xlsx, 005 docx)
additionally use NCAA Baylor Bears / Baylor Bears Font display type and
Bahnschrift body, with a black masthead bar. Those fonts render only on a
machine that has them installed; Word substitutes elsewhere.

---

## 7. Telemetry platform notes

Telemetry Sports (app.telemetry.fm, branded Teamworks) is the recruiting and
scouting platform. Login is the user's; an agent without a browser session
cannot reach it.

- **Transfer Portal** > Player Traits / Advanced Stats / Boxscore. Traits and
  stats appear only after filtering to a position or position group.
- **Scout Reports > Settings** holds the Player Grade dropdown, already loaded
  with the six STAQS tiers. Scout reports carry a numeric Score (0-72) plus the
  grade.

# New Telemetry traits and the young-player weight rule

Date: 2026-10-17. Status: **decisions recorded; build in 020.** Nothing in
019 changed.

## What Telemetry added

Read from the live leaderboard Columns panel (2026, all 11 groups, both tabs)
on 2026-10-17. Advanced Stats: no change. Player Traits: 7 new columns.

| Group | New Player Traits columns |
|---|---|
| OT, IOL | Pull Agility, Perimeter Speed |
| OB-LB | Closing, Reaction Time |
| CB, SAF | Targeted Coverage, Closing, Reaction Time |

Telemetry's own definitions (player-page tooltips):

| Trait | Definition |
|---|---|
| Pull Agility | Measures a lineman's ability to change direction and cut upfield as a puller. |
| Perimeter Speed | Measures a lineman's straight line speed. |
| Targeted Coverage | Measures the primary coverage defender's ability to stay in phase when targeted. |
| Closing | Measures a defender's ability to close on the ball when it's in the air, both as the primary and secondary defender. |
| Reaction Time | Measures how fast a secondary defender commits to the ball once it's thrown. |

LB tooltips were not read separately; assumed the same text.

**Sample size:** these traits are blank for many players. On the OT board,
4 of the top 15 have no Pull Agility / Perimeter Speed. One 2026 CB ranked
"14th of 36 in FBS" on Reaction Time, so very few players are scored.

## Effect on the pipeline today

- `check_exports.py` flags only missing columns, so the new columns pass.
- `scripts/powerquery/Stage.m` keeps only its known column list, so the new
  columns are dropped silently. Nothing breaks; nothing is used.

## Crosswalk (confirmed; add as secondaries, not counted traits)

Counted traits drive elite share (same open question as Elusiveness), so
these go in as secondaries until that is decided.

| Group | Trait | Baylor factor (000 GRD SCALE) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| OT | Pull Agility | Athletic Ability | Factor had no Telemetry feed (no CoD/Decel for OL). |
| OT | Perimeter Speed | Speed (Play-speed) | Colleague proposed Foot speed / Redirect. The definition is straight-line speed, so Speed. Speed had no OL feed. |
| OG/C | Pull Agility | Pulling / 2nd level blocking | Direct match. |
| OG/C | Perimeter Speed | Speed (Play-speed) | As OT. |
| CB, STAR | Targeted Coverage | Man-to-Man Coverage | Direct match. |
| CB, STAR | Closing | Ball Skills | "Disruptive at rec. point." |
| CB, STAR | Reaction Time | Ball Skills (secondary) | No read/react factor on CB. |
| SAF | Reaction Time | Key & Diagnose | "Reads and reacts quickly." |
| SAF | Closing | Range | Plays to the sideline. |
| SAF | Targeted Coverage | none clean | Info only until staff decide. |
| LB | Closing | Lateral quickness / Range | Weak fit. |
| LB | Reaction Time | none | LB scale has no read/react factor. Info only. |

All rows confirmed by Eric, 2026-10-17.

## Weight rule for young players (Eric chose option 1, 2026-10-17)

Height stays the hard line. A player whose only size miss is weight below the
SETTINGS floor, with Elig. 3 or more, is flagged **PROJECT** instead of
scoring Size 1 (critical deficiency). Older players keep the current rule:
a light senior is not a project.

below-floor weight scores today (1 or 3). The 000 matrix weight columns were
unclear in the text export. `check_workbook.py` does not recompute SIZE, so
spot-check SIZE and the PROJECT flag on a few players per position.

## Build list for 020

1. Stage.m and POSITION MAP: add the 7 columns (OT, IOL, OB-LB, CB, SAF).
2. CROSSWALK / glossary: add the rows above, with the definitions.
3. SIZE: weight-only miss + Elig. >= 3 -> PROJECT, not 1.
4. `check_exports.py`: add the new columns to EXPECTED only after a full
   2023-2026 pull shows whether older seasons carry them.

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

Opening files through `~/Library/CloudStorage/GoogleDrive-…/My Drive/` hangs when the file is
not cached locally. Measured 2026-10-14: a sha256 walk of `_FROM_WORK_LAPTOP` sat 65 minutes with

folder is 0 KB on disk — all cloud placeholders). `stat()` and `os.walk` are fine: five Drive
folders, 76k files, 10 seconds by name+size.

(thousands of face images). Skip it in any Drive walk.

- Move or rename Drive folders with the Drive MCP (`update_file` with `parentId`) — server-side, instant,
  no FUSE. Never `mv` a big tree through the mount.
- Put any Drive walk under a wall-clock watchdog; a hang shows as elapsed time with no CPU.
- Related: [[drive-fuse-rsync-mtime-loop]] (rsync re-sends), [[rea-ghidra-setup-traps]] (Drive reads hang R).

**Moving Drive items (2026-10-14 evening):** the Claude Code permission classifier can block the Drive MCP
`update_file` move as "Modify Shared Resources" even after it has worked in the same session. The gws CLI
(`/opt/homebrew/bin/gws`, Drive scope granted) does the same server-side move from the shell and is not blocked:
`gws drive files update --params '{"fileId":"<id>","addParents":"<new>","removeParents":"<old>","fields":"id,name,parents"}' --json '{}'`.
Uploads with `--upload` must name a file under the current directory (`cd` to the job tmp dir first).

input.content:
"""patch-mashup: replace the Power Query M in a workbook without Excel COM (Mac builds, 020 on).

Every workbook up to 019 set wb.Queries(name).Formula through Excel COM on
Windows. Mac Excel has no such object model, so this rewrites the M directly
inside the file: customXml/item1.xml holds the DataMashup (base64), whose
package zip holds Formulas/Section1.m. Each query in Section1.m is rebuilt from
scripts/powerquery/<name>.m. Permissions, metadata and the rest of the xlsx are
copied byte for byte. The permission bindings stay as they were; Excel treats
bindings that no longer match as absent.

Refuses to overwrite --out. Run before any Excel edits, then open --out in
Excel (Refresh All, save) so Excel rewrites the file itself.

Usage:
  uv run python scripts/patch_mashup.py --src "<019>.xlsx" --out "<work>/020_step1.xlsx"
"""

import argparse
import base64
import io
import re
import struct
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

PQ = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "powerquery"
QUERIES = ["Stage", "PortalInput", "LoadStatus"]  # order in Section1.m


def section_m():
    parts = [f"shared {n} = " + (PQ / f"{n}.m").read_text(encoding="utf-8").rstrip() + "\n;" for n in QUERIES]
    return "section Section1;\r\n\r\n" + "\r\n\r\n".join(parts)


def patch_mashup(blob: bytes, new_m: str) -> tuple[bytes, str]:
    ver, plen = struct.unpack("<II", blob[:8])
    pkg, rest = blob[8:8 + plen], blob[8 + plen:]
    src = zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(pkg))
    old_m = src.read("Formulas/Section1.m").decode("utf-8-sig")
    names_old = re.findall(r"^shared (\S+?) =", old_m, re.M)
    if names_old != QUERIES:

"""add-new-traits: build 020 on the Mac from patch_mashup.py output (Mac Excel via xlwings).

Telemetry added five Player Traits in October 2026 (Pull Agility, Perimeter
Speed on OT/IOL; Closing, Reaction Time on OB-LB; Targeted Coverage, Closing,
Reaction Time on CB/SAF). Decisions: docs/2026-10-17-new-telemetry-traits.md.
020 changes:
- Power Query Stage (done by patch_mashup.py): the five land on PORTAL INPUT
  after BT as secondary metrics; a Mac folder path (/...) also loads.
- CROSSWALK: the five added as secondary metrics on the factors Eric confirmed.
- METRIC GLOSSARY: five rows with Telemetry's own definitions.
- SETTINGS row 59: PROJECT minimum Elig Yrs (3).
- REVIEW BOARD AR "Project": PROJECT when height is at the position's 9 line,
  weight is under the ideal band and Elig Yrs is at least SETTINGS B59.
  Information only: no other formula reads it, SIZE (data) is unchanged.
- README: a note on the above.
The workbook is refreshed on the 44 2025 CSVs 019 shipped with, so every
player value should be unchanged; the export folder cell is left empty.

Mac only. Refuses to overwrite --out.

Usage:
  uv run --with xlwings python scripts/add_new_traits.py --src "<work>/020_step1.xlsx" \
      --out "<work>/020 ....xlsx" --stage "<work>/load_2025"
"""

import argparse
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

LAST_RB_ROW = 20004

# (CROSSWALK row, new Secondary metrics F, text appended to Data flag rule H or None)
CROSSWALK = [
    (31, "Deceleration (WR, CB, S); Pull Agility (OT)", None),
    (33, "Perimeter Speed, Movement",
     " Perimeter Speed (Telemetry 2026: straight-line speed) supports; secondary only."),
    (41, "Perimeter Speed, Movement",
     " Perimeter Speed (Telemetry 2026: straight-line speed) supports; secondary only."),
    (43, "Pull Agility, Run Blocking, Disruption Prevention", None),
    (75, "Play Speed, Deep Speed, Screen Awareness, Closing", None),
    (82, "Targeted Coverage, Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", None),
    (84, "Completion Rate Over Expected, Closing, Reaction Time", None),
    (90, "Deep Speed, Adjusted Speed, CoD, Closing", None),
    (91, "Reaction Time, Target Rate, EPA Per Target", None),
    (98, "Targeted Coverage, Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", None),
    (100, "Completion Rate Over Expected, Closing, Reaction Time", None),
]
# Row 33 / 41 checks: the F text these rows carried in 019.
CROSSWALK_WAS = {31: "Deceleration (WR, CB, S)", 33: "Movement", 41: "Movement",
                 43: "Run Blocking, Disruption Prevention", 75: "Play Speed, Deep Speed, Screen Awareness",
                 82: "Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", 84: "Completion Rate Over Expected",
                 90: "Deep Speed, Adjusted Speed, CoD", 91: "Target Rate, EPA Per Target",
                 98: "Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", 100: "Completion Rate Over Expected"}

GLOSSARY = [
    ["Pull Agility", "Player Traits", "IOL, OT",
     "Telemetry: a lineman's ability to change direction and cut upfield as a puller. Added 2026; blank for many players.",
     "Pulling / 2nd Level (OG, C); Athletic Flexibility (OT). Secondary."],
    ["Perimeter Speed", "Player Traits", "IOL, OT",
     "Telemetry: a lineman's straight line speed. Added 2026; blank for many players.",
     "Speed (critical), OL. Secondary."],
    ["Targeted Coverage", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF",
     "Telemetry: the primary coverage defender's ability to stay in phase when targeted. Added 2026.",
     "Man-to-Man Coverage (CB, STAR). Secondary."],
    ["Closing", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF, LB",
     "Telemetry: a defender's ability to close on the ball in the air, as primary and secondary defender. Added 2026.",
     "Ball Skills (CB, STAR); Range (SAF); Lateral Quickness / Range (LB). Secondary."],
    ["Reaction Time", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF, LB",
     "Telemetry: how fast a secondary defender commits to the ball once it is thrown. Added 2026; few players scored.",
     "Key & Diagnose (SAF); Ball Skills (CB, STAR). Secondary."],
]

SETTING = ["PROJECT flag: minimum Elig Yrs", 3,
           "REVIEW BOARD Project column: PROJECT when height is at the 9 line, weight is under the ideal band and "
           "Elig Yrs is at least this. Information only; SIZE (data) is unchanged (weight only decides 9 vs 3)."]

P = "'PORTAL INPUT'!"
LOOK = "MATCH({p}B5,SETTINGS!$A$27:$A$38,0)".format(p=P)
PROJECT = (f'=IF({P}A5="","",IFERROR(IF(AND(ISNUMBER({P}E5),ISNUMBER({P}F5),'
           f'{P}E5>=INDEX(SETTINGS!$B$27:$B$38,{LOOK}),'
           f'{P}F5<INDEX(SETTINGS!$D$27:$D$38,{LOOK}),'
           f'N({P}G5)>=SETTINGS!$B$59),"PROJECT",""),""))')

README_ADD = (" 020: Telemetry's 2026 traits (Pull Agility, Perimeter Speed, Targeted Coverage, Closing, Reaction "
              "Time) load after BT as secondary metrics; they do not change elite share. REVIEW BOARD column AR "
              "flags PROJECT: tall enough for a 9, under the weight band, Elig Yrs at least SETTINGS B59.")


def wait_refresh(ud, before, timeout=1200):
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < timeout:
        time.sleep(10)
        now = ud.range("B16").value
        if now and now != before:
            time.sleep(10)
            return time.time() - t0
    raise SystemExit("Refresh did not finish")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--src", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--stage", required=True, help="local folder with the CSVs to refresh on")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out)
    if out.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite {out}")
    shutil.copy2(args.src, out)

    import xlwings as xw
    app = xw.App(visible=True, add_book=False)
    app.display_alerts = False
    try:
        wb = app.books.open(str(out))

        cw = wb.sheets["CROSSWALK"]
        for row, f, h_add in CROSSWALK:
            was = cw.range(f"F{row}").value
            if was != CROSSWALK_WAS[row]:
                raise SystemExit(f"CROSSWALK F{row} reads {was!r}, expected {CROSSWALK_WAS[row]!r}")
            cw.range(f"F{row}").value = f
            if h_add:
                cw.range(f"H{row}").value = cw.range(f"H{row}").value + h_add

        mg = wb.sheets["METRIC GLOSSARY"]
        if mg.range("A52").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("METRIC GLOSSARY row 52 is not empty")
        mg.range("A51:H51").copy(mg.range("A52:H56"))
        mg.range("A52").value = GLOSSARY

        st = wb.sheets["SETTINGS"]
        if st.range("A59").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("SETTINGS row 59 is not empty")
        st.range("A58:C58").copy(st.range("A59:C59"))
        st.range("A59").value = [SETTING]

        rb = wb.sheets["REVIEW BOARD"]
        if rb.range("AR4").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("REVIEW BOARD AR4 is not empty")
        rb.range(f"AQ4:AQ{LAST_RB_ROW}").copy(rb.range("AR4"))
        rb.range("AR4").value = "Project"
        rb.range(f"AR5:AR{LAST_RB_ROW}").formula = PROJECT

        readme = wb.sheets["README"]
        cell = readme.used_range.api.find(what="PORTAL INPUT is filled by Power Query")
        if cell is None:
            raise SystemExit("README DATA LOAD note not found")
        addr = cell.get_address(row_absolute=False, column_absolute=False)
        txt = readme.range(addr).value
        if README_ADD.strip() not in txt:
            readme.range(addr).value = txt + README_ADD

        ud = wb.sheets["UPDATE DATA"]
        folder = wb.names["LoadFolder"].refers_to_range
        folder.value = str(Path(args.stage)) + "/"
        before = ud.range("B16").value
        wb.api.refresh_all()
        print(f"Refresh All: {wait_refresh(ud, before):.0f} s")
        folder.value = ""  # shipped empty
        for item, value in ud.range("A16:B26").value:
            print(f"  {item}: {str(value)[:160]}")
        wb.save()
        wb.close()
    finally:
        app.quit()
    print(f"saved {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""add-new-traits: build 020 on the Mac from patch_mashup.py output (Mac Excel via xlwings).

Telemetry added five Player Traits in October 2026 (Pull Agility, Perimeter
Speed on OT/IOL; Closing, Reaction Time on OB-LB; Targeted Coverage, Closing,
Reaction Time on CB/SAF). Decisions: docs/2026-10-17-new-telemetry-traits.md.
020 changes:
- Power Query Stage (done by patch_mashup.py): the five land on PORTAL INPUT
  after BT as secondary metrics; a Mac folder path (/...) also loads.
- CROSSWALK: the five added as secondary metrics on the factors Eric confirmed.
- METRIC GLOSSARY: five rows with Telemetry's own definitions.
- SETTINGS row 59: PROJECT minimum Elig Yrs (3).
- REVIEW BOARD AR "Project": PROJECT when height is at the position's 9 line,
  weight is under the ideal band and Elig Yrs is at least SETTINGS B59.
  Information only: no other formula reads it, SIZE (data) is unchanged.
- README: a note on the above.
The workbook is refreshed on the 44 2025 CSVs 019 shipped with, so every
player value should be unchanged; the export folder cell is left empty.

Mac only. Refuses to overwrite --out.

Usage:
  uv run --with xlwings python scripts/add_new_traits.py --src "<work>/020_step1.xlsx" \
      --out "<work>/020 ....xlsx" --stage "<work>/load_2025"
"""

import argparse
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

LAST_RB_ROW = 20004

# (CROSSWALK row, new Secondary metrics F, text appended to Data flag rule H or None)
CROSSWALK = [
    (31, "Deceleration (WR, CB, S); Pull Agility (OT)", None),
    (33, "Perimeter Speed, Movement",
     " Perimeter Speed (Telemetry 2026: straight-line speed) supports; secondary only."),
    (41, "Perimeter Speed, Movement",
     " Perimeter Speed (Telemetry 2026: straight-line speed) supports; secondary only."),
    (43, "Pull Agility, Run Blocking, Disruption Prevention", None),
    (75, "Play Speed, Deep Speed, Screen Awareness, Closing", None),
    (82, "Targeted Coverage, Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", None),
    (84, "Completion Rate Over Expected, Closing, Reaction Time", None),
    (90, "Deep Speed, Adjusted Speed, CoD, Closing", None),
    (91, "Reaction Time, Target Rate, EPA Per Target", None),
    (98, "Targeted Coverage, Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", None),
    (100, "Completion Rate Over Expected, Closing, Reaction Time", None),
]
# Row 33 / 41 checks: the F text these rows carried in 019.
CROSSWALK_WAS = {31: "Deceleration (WR, CB, S)", 33: "Movement", 41: "Movement",
                 43: "Run Blocking, Disruption Prevention", 75: "Play Speed, Deep Speed, Screen Awareness",
                 82: "Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", 84: "Completion Rate Over Expected",
                 90: "Deep Speed, Adjusted Speed, CoD", 91: "Target Rate, EPA Per Target",
                 98: "Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", 100: "Completion Rate Over Expected"}

GLOSSARY = [
    ["Pull Agility", "Player Traits", "IOL, OT",
     "Telemetry: a lineman's ability to change direction and cut upfield as a puller. Added 2026; blank for many players.",
     "Pulling / 2nd Level (OG, C); Athletic Flexibility (OT). Secondary."],
    ["Perimeter Speed", "Player Traits", "IOL, OT",
     "Telemetry: a lineman's straight line speed. Added 2026; blank for many players.",
     "Speed (critical), OL. Secondary."],
    ["Targeted Coverage", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF",
     "Telemetry: the primary coverage defender's ability to stay in phase when targeted. Added 2026.",
     "Man-to-Man Coverage (CB, STAR). Secondary."],
    ["Closing", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF, LB",
     "Telemetry: a defender's ability to close on the ball in the air, as primary and secondary defender. Added 2026.",
     "Ball Skills (CB, STAR); Range (SAF); Lateral Quickness / Range (LB). Secondary."],
    ["Reaction Time", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF, LB",
     "Telemetry: how fast a secondary defender commits to the ball once it is thrown. Added 2026; few players scored.",
     "Key & Diagnose (SAF); Ball Skills (CB, STAR). Secondary."],
]

SETTING = ["PROJECT flag: minimum Elig Yrs", 3,
           "REVIEW BOARD Project column: PROJECT when height is at the 9 line, weight is under the ideal band and "
           "Elig Yrs is at least this. Information only; SIZE (data) is unchanged (weight only decides 9 vs 3)."]

P = "'PORTAL INPUT'!"
LOOK = "MATCH({p}B5,SETTINGS!$A$27:$A$38,0)".format(p=P)
PROJECT = (f'=IF({P}A5="","",IFERROR(IF(AND(ISNUMBER({P}E5),ISNUMBER({P}F5),'
           f'{P}E5>=INDEX(SETTINGS!$B$27:$B$38,{LOOK}),'
           f'{P}F5<INDEX(SETTINGS!$D$27:$D$38,{LOOK}),'
           f'N({P}G5)>=SETTINGS!$B$59),"PROJECT",""),""))')

README_ADD = (" 020: Telemetry's 2026 traits (Pull Agility, Perimeter Speed, Targeted Coverage, Closing, Reaction "
              "Time) load after BT as secondary metrics; they do not change elite share. REVIEW BOARD column AR "
              "flags PROJECT: tall enough for a 9, under the weight band, Elig Yrs at least SETTINGS B59.")


def wait_refresh(ud, before, timeout=1200):
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < timeout:
        time.sleep(10)
        now = ud.range("B16").value
        if now and now != before:
            time.sleep(10)
            return time.time() - t0
    raise SystemExit("Refresh did not finish")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--src", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--stage", required=True, help="local folder with the CSVs to refresh on")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out)
    if out.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite {out}")
    shutil.copy2(args.src, out)

    import xlwings as xw
    app = xw.App(visible=True, add_book=False)
    app.display_alerts = False
    try:
        wb = app.books.open(str(out))

        cw = wb.sheets["CROSSWALK"]
        for row, f, h_add in CROSSWALK:
            was = cw.range(f"F{row}").value
            if was != CROSSWALK_WAS[row]:
                raise SystemExit(f"CROSSWALK F{row} reads {was!r}, expected {CROSSWALK_WAS[row]!r}")
            cw.range(f"F{row}").value = f
            if h_add:
                cw.range(f"H{row}").value = cw.range(f"H{row}").value + h_add

        mg = wb.sheets["METRIC GLOSSARY"]
        if mg.range("A52").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("METRIC GLOSSARY row 52 is not empty")
        mg.range("A51:H51").copy(mg.range("A52:H56"))
        mg.range("A52").value = GLOSSARY

        st = wb.sheets["SETTINGS"]
        if st.range("A59").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("SETTINGS row 59 is not empty")
        st.range("A58:C58").copy(st.range("A59:C59"))
        st.range("A59").value = [SETTING]

        rb = wb.sheets["REVIEW BOARD"]
        if rb.range("AR4").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("REVIEW BOARD AR4 is not empty")
        rb.range(f"AQ4:AQ{LAST_RB_ROW}").copy(rb.range("AR4"))
        rb.range("AR4").value = "Project"
        rb.range(f"AR5:AR{LAST_RB_ROW}").formula = PROJECT

        readme = wb.sheets["README"]
        used = readme.used_range
        hits = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(used.value) for c, v in enumerate(row)
                if isinstance(v, str) and "PORTAL INPUT is filled by Power Query" in v]
        if len(hits) != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"README DATA LOAD note found {len(hits)} times")
        addr = used[hits[0][0], hits[0][1]].address
        txt = readme.range(addr).value
        if README_ADD.strip() not in txt:
            readme.range(addr).value = txt + README_ADD

        ud = wb.sheets["UPDATE DATA"]
        folder = wb.names["LoadFolder"].refers_to_range
        folder.value = str(Path(args.stage)) + "/"
        before = ud.range("B16").value
        wb.api.refresh_all()
        print(f"Refresh All: {wait_refresh(ud, before):.0f} s")
        folder.value = ""  # shipped empty
        for item, value in ud.range("A16:B26").value:
            print(f"  {item}: {str(value)[:160]}")
        wb.save()
        wb.close()
    finally:
        app.quit()
    print(f"saved {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Validate a grading workbook (009 layout) against the documented algorithm.

Read only; never writes the workbook. Checks, each reported PASS or FAIL:

1. tabs          all eight tabs present, in order (BENCHMARK PROFILES may follow)
2. settings      SETTINGS labels at the cells the formulas use (B5:B12, band
                 table A17:A20), values numeric
3. headers       PORTAL INPUT and REVIEW BOARD headers where the fixed-position
                 formulas expect them
4. formulas      key REVIEW BOARD formulas point at the right SETTINGS cells, and
                 every data row carries the same formula as row 5 (no hand edits)
5. errors        no #REF!, #VALUE! or other error values on REVIEW BOARD
6. cond-format   REVIEW BOARD conditional formatting present, alert highlight
                 covers L:O
7. recompute     every row's Traits graded, Elite traits, Deficiencies, Elite
                 share, Projected band, Sample, Speed alert, Impact alert,
                 REVIEW? and Low Impact alert recomputed in Python from PORTAL
                 INPUT + SETTINGS (AGENTS.md section 5) and compared with the
                 values Excel calculated. From 013 on (REVIEW BOARD has a
                 "Profile REVIEW" column), the position-profile columns and the
                 profile path into REVIEW are recomputed too (add_profiles.py)

Exit code 0 only if every check passes. The workbook must have been saved by
Excel (cached values present), which every build script here does.

Usage:
  uv run --with openpyxl python scripts/check_workbook.py <workbook.xlsx> [--max-report 10]
"""

import argparse

119:    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])

121:    ap.add_argument("--max-report", type=int, default=10)

"""add-new-traits: build 020 on the Mac from patch_mashup.py output (Mac Excel via xlwings).

Telemetry added five Player Traits in October 2026 (Pull Agility, Perimeter
Speed on OT/IOL; Closing, Reaction Time on OB-LB; Targeted Coverage, Closing,
Reaction Time on CB/SAF). Decisions: docs/2026-10-17-new-telemetry-traits.md.
020 changes:
- Power Query Stage (done by patch_mashup.py): the five land on PORTAL INPUT
  after BT as secondary metrics; a Mac folder path (/...) also loads.
- CROSSWALK: the five added as secondary metrics on the factors Eric confirmed.
- METRIC GLOSSARY: five rows with Telemetry's own definitions.
- SETTINGS row 59: PROJECT minimum Elig Yrs (3).
- REVIEW BOARD AR "Project": PROJECT when height is at the position's 9 line,
  weight is under the ideal band and Elig Yrs is at least SETTINGS B59.
  Information only: no other formula reads it, SIZE (data) is unchanged.
- README: a note on the above.
The workbook is refreshed on the 44 2025 CSVs 019 shipped with, so every
player value should be unchanged; the export folder cell is left empty.

Mac only. Refuses to overwrite --out.

Usage:
  uv run --with xlwings python scripts/add_new_traits.py --src "<work>/020_step1.xlsx" \
      --out "<work>/020 ....xlsx" --stage "<work>/load_2025"
"""

import argparse
import shutil
import time
from pathlib import Path

LAST_RB_ROW = 20004

# (CROSSWALK row, new Secondary metrics F, text appended to Data flag rule H or None)
CROSSWALK = [
    (31, "Deceleration (WR, CB, S); Pull Agility (OT)", None),
    (33, "Perimeter Speed, Movement",
     " Perimeter Speed (Telemetry 2026: straight-line speed) supports; secondary only."),
    (41, "Perimeter Speed, Movement",
     " Perimeter Speed (Telemetry 2026: straight-line speed) supports; secondary only."),
    (43, "Pull Agility, Run Blocking, Disruption Prevention", None),
    (75, "Play Speed, Deep Speed, Screen Awareness, Closing", None),
    (82, "Targeted Coverage, Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", None),
    (84, "Completion Rate Over Expected, Closing, Reaction Time", None),
    (90, "Deep Speed, Adjusted Speed, CoD, Closing", None),
    (91, "Reaction Time, Target Rate, EPA Per Target", None),
    (98, "Targeted Coverage, Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", None),
    (100, "Completion Rate Over Expected, Closing, Reaction Time", None),
]
# Row 33 / 41 checks: the F text these rows carried in 019.
CROSSWALK_WAS = {31: "Deceleration (WR, CB, S)", 33: "Movement", 41: "Movement",
                 43: "Run Blocking, Disruption Prevention", 75: "Play Speed, Deep Speed, Screen Awareness",
                 82: "Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", 84: "Completion Rate Over Expected",
                 90: "Deep Speed, Adjusted Speed, CoD", 91: "Target Rate, EPA Per Target",
                 98: "Completion Rate Over Expected, Target Rate", 100: "Completion Rate Over Expected"}

GLOSSARY = [
    ["Pull Agility", "Player Traits", "IOL, OT",
     "Telemetry: a lineman's ability to change direction and cut upfield as a puller. Added 2026; blank for many players.",
     "Pulling / 2nd Level (OG, C); Athletic Flexibility (OT). Secondary."],
    ["Perimeter Speed", "Player Traits", "IOL, OT",
     "Telemetry: a lineman's straight line speed. Added 2026; blank for many players.",
     "Speed (critical), OL. Secondary."],
    ["Targeted Coverage", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF",
     "Telemetry: the primary coverage defender's ability to stay in phase when targeted. Added 2026.",
     "Man-to-Man Coverage (CB, STAR). Secondary."],
    ["Closing", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF, LB",
     "Telemetry: a defender's ability to close on the ball in the air, as primary and secondary defender. Added 2026.",
     "Ball Skills (CB, STAR); Range (SAF); Lateral Quickness / Range (LB). Secondary."],
    ["Reaction Time", "Player Traits", "CB, SAF, LB",
     "Telemetry: how fast a secondary defender commits to the ball once it is thrown. Added 2026; few players scored.",
     "Key & Diagnose (SAF); Ball Skills (CB, STAR). Secondary."],
]

SETTING = ["PROJECT flag: minimum Elig Yrs", 3,
           "REVIEW BOARD Project column: PROJECT when height is at the 9 line, weight is under the ideal band and "
           "Elig Yrs is at least this. Information only; SIZE (data) is unchanged (weight only decides 9 vs 3)."]

P = "'PORTAL INPUT'!"
LOOK = "MATCH({p}B5,SETTINGS!$A$27:$A$38,0)".format(p=P)
PROJECT = (f'=IF({P}A5="","",IFERROR(IF(AND(ISNUMBER({P}E5),ISNUMBER({P}F5),'
           f'{P}E5>=INDEX(SETTINGS!$B$27:$B$38,{LOOK}),'
           f'{P}F5<INDEX(SETTINGS!$D$27:$D$38,{LOOK}),'
           f'N({P}G5)>=SETTINGS!$B$59),"PROJECT",""),""))')

README_ADD = (" 020: Telemetry's 2026 traits (Pull Agility, Perimeter Speed, Targeted Coverage, Closing, Reaction "
              "Time) load after BT as secondary metrics; they do not change elite share. REVIEW BOARD column AR "
              "flags PROJECT: tall enough for a 9, under the weight band, Elig Yrs at least SETTINGS B59.")


def wait_refresh(ud, before, timeout=1200):
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < timeout:
        time.sleep(10)
        try:
            now = ud.range("B16").value
        except Exception:  # Excel answers -1728 while a refresh is running
            continue
        if now and now != before:
            time.sleep(10)
            return time.time() - t0
    raise SystemExit("Refresh did not finish")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--src", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--stage", required=True, help="local folder with the CSVs to refresh on")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out)
    if out.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite {out}")
    shutil.copy2(args.src, out)

    import xlwings as xw
    app = xw.App(visible=True, add_book=False)
    app.display_alerts = False
    try:
        wb = app.books.open(str(out))

        cw = wb.sheets["CROSSWALK"]
        for row, f, h_add in CROSSWALK:
            was = cw.range(f"F{row}").value
            if was != CROSSWALK_WAS[row]:
                raise SystemExit(f"CROSSWALK F{row} reads {was!r}, expected {CROSSWALK_WAS[row]!r}")
            cw.range(f"F{row}").value = f
            if h_add:
                cw.range(f"H{row}").value = cw.range(f"H{row}").value + h_add

        mg = wb.sheets["METRIC GLOSSARY"]
        if mg.range("A52").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("METRIC GLOSSARY row 52 is not empty")
        mg.range("A51:H51").copy(mg.range("A52:H56"))
        mg.range("A52").value = GLOSSARY

        st = wb.sheets["SETTINGS"]
        if st.range("A59").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("SETTINGS row 59 is not empty")
        st.range("A58:C58").copy(st.range("A59:C59"))
        st.range("A59").value = [SETTING]

        rb = wb.sheets["REVIEW BOARD"]
        if rb.range("AR4").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("REVIEW BOARD AR4 is not empty")
        rb.range(f"AQ4:AQ{LAST_RB_ROW}").copy(rb.range("AR4"))
        rb.range("AR4").value = "Project"
        rb.range(f"AR5:AR{LAST_RB_ROW}").formula = PROJECT

        readme = wb.sheets["README"]
        used = readme.used_range
        hits = [(r, c) for r, row in enumerate(used.value) for c, v in enumerate(row)
                if isinstance(v, str) and "PORTAL INPUT is filled by Power Query" in v]
        if len(hits) != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"README DATA LOAD note found {len(hits)} times")
        addr = used[hits[0][0], hits[0][1]].address
        txt = readme.range(addr).value
        if README_ADD.strip() not in txt:
            readme.range(addr).value = txt + README_ADD

        ud = wb.sheets["UPDATE DATA"]
        folder = wb.names["LoadFolder"].refers_to_range
        folder.value = str(Path(args.stage)) + "/"
        before = ud.range("B16").value
        wb.api.refresh_all()
        print(f"Refresh All: {wait_refresh(ud, before):.0f} s")
        folder.value = ""  # shipped empty
        for item, value in ud.range("A16:B26").value:
            print(f"  {item}: {str(value)[:160]}")
        wb.save()
        wb.close()
    finally:
        app.quit()
    print(f"saved {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def wait_refresh(ud, before, timeout=1200):
    t0 = time.time()
    while time.time() - t0 < timeout:
        time.sleep(10)
        try:
            now = ud.range("B16").value
        except Exception:  # Excel answers -1728 while a refresh is running
            continue
        if now and now != before:
            time.sleep(10)
            return time.time() - t0
    raise SystemExit("Refresh did not finish")


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.splitlines()[0])
    ap.add_argument("--src", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--stage", required=True, help="local folder with the CSVs to refresh on")
    args = ap.parse_args()
    out = Path(args.out)
    if out.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"Refusing to overwrite {out}")
    shutil.copy2(args.src, out)

    import xlwings as xw
    app = xw.App(visible=True, add_book=False)
    app.display_alerts = False
    try:
        wb = app.books.open(str(out))

        cw = wb.sheets["CROSSWALK"]
        for row, f, h_add in CROSSWALK:
            was = cw.range(f"F{row}").value
            if was != CROSSWALK_WAS[row]:
                raise SystemExit(f"CROSSWALK F{row} reads {was!r}, expected {CROSSWALK_WAS[row]!r}")
            cw.range(f"F{row}").value = f
            if h_add:
                cw.range(f"H{row}").value = cw.range(f"H{row}").value + h_add

        mg = wb.sheets["METRIC GLOSSARY"]
        if mg.range("A52").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("METRIC GLOSSARY row 52 is not empty")
        mg.range("A51:H51").copy(mg.range("A52:H56"))
        mg.range("A52").value = GLOSSARY

        st = wb.sheets["SETTINGS"]
        if st.range("A59").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("SETTINGS row 59 is not empty")
        st.range("A58:C58").copy(st.range("A59:C59"))
        st.range("A59").value = [SETTING]

        rb = wb.sheets["REVIEW BOARD"]
        if rb.range("AR4").value is not None:
            raise SystemExit("REVIEW BOARD AR4 is not empty")
        rb.range(f"AQ4:AQ{LAST_RB_ROW}").copy(rb.range("AR4"))
